findings.title: Markets and instruments are plain data with validation at construction
findings.description:
`Market`, `SessionCalendarRef`, `ContractTerms` and `Instrument` are frozen, slotted dataclasses. Each declares `CANONICAL_TYPE` and `SCHEMA_VERSION`, which `canonical.py` requires for dataclasses.

`__post_init__` rejects bad input with specific `CoreModelError` subclasses. Examples are `float` or `bool` for numeric terms, `Decimal` NaN or infinity, lowercase or newline-suffixed currency codes, and `str` subclasses as instrument ids.

`Market` normalizes its unordered inputs into canonical order. `session_calendars` becomes a tuple sorted by mode, and `adjustment_bases` becomes a frozenset. Equal markets therefore hash and canonicalize identically, and `test_equal_markets_in_different_order_canonicalize_to_equal_bytes` covers this.

All enums are `StrEnum`, which `canonical.py` accepts. Values such as the source-bar-stamping set are defined once, in `SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS`.

findings.title: Tests cover behavior, identity and the module boundary
findings.description:
The tests are parametrized over rejection cases and fixture values. Identity is tested one fact at a time: each row of `CHANGED_FACTS` changes exactly one fact and must change the hash.

`test_market_uniformity.py` runs one code path for every market. The golden vectors were computed independently of `canonical_hash`. `test_import_boundary.py` now covers `markets.py` and `instruments.py`. The fixture calendar mapping is checked for immutability and for keys matching each calendar's own id.

findings.title: `_require_instance` is duplicated across modules
findings.description: `instruments.py` and `markets.py` each define a private `_require_instance`. The two differ only in which exception they raise. A shared helper that takes the error type would remove the copy. The cost of leaving it is small, but it is a DRY drift risk if the message format changes in one file only.

findings.title: Unhashable input to `Market` raises `TypeError`, not `InvalidMarketError`
findings.description: `self.source_bar_stamping not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` and `frozenset(bases)` both hash their input. Unhashable values, such as a list passed as the stamping or as an element of `adjustment_bases`, raise a bare `TypeError` instead of the module's own `InvalidMarketError`. Checking `isinstance(..., TimeMeaning)` first would give a consistent error contract. This only affects callers that already violate the static types.

findings.title: `Market` field annotations are narrower than the accepted inputs
findings.description: The docstring says `session_calendars` and `adjustment_bases` accept any iterable. The field annotations are `tuple[...]` and `frozenset[...]`, so strict pyright flags list and generator arguments. The tests work around this by building kwargs as `dict[str, Any]`. This is acceptable because the stored form is the annotated one, but a custom `__init__` or a factory classmethod would make the contract explicit.

structured_findings.summary: Markets and instruments are plain data with validation at construction
Tests cover behavior, identity and the module boundary
`Market` field annotations are narrower than the accepted inputs
